data.description:
As a maintainer, I want a structurally-accurate (ast-grep / sg) dangling-reference matcher with a measured false-positive rate so that enforcing dangling-references does not wedge legitimate promotions on comment/string false matches.

Plan refs: A-4 (CF-8); the matcher is git-grep today (check-dangling-references.sh:20-21 — confirmed greenfield). E7 is BLOCKING for the enforce-flip. THIS IS THE EPIC'S ONE GENUINE REBUILD-RISK — front-loaded so we learn the answer fast.

DONE DEFINITION:
- DD1: sg-based reference matcher (guarded git-grep fallback when sg absent), reference-side scans .md/.yml/Makefile/.txt, short-symbol guard. (SC1)
- DD2: a 20-PR ground-truth set is assembled and the matcher's FP/FN rate measured against it. (SC1)
- DD3: GO/NO-GO recorded: FP rate 0 (or acceptable) -> dangling-references is enforce-ready; OTHERWISE the documented FALLBACK applies (ship review-gate with coverage-invariant ENFORCED and dangling-references ADVISORY) and the epic proceeds with reduced scope, not blocked.
- DD4: TDD for the matcher + the fallback wiring.

LIVE VERIFICATION + EXPERIMENTS:
- E7: run the matcher over the 20-PR ground-truth set; record FP/FN. Also confirm its exit-78 enforce path blocks (mirror of story 1, V0.4).

COURSE-CORRECTION TRIGGER (the key fast-feedback gate): if sg cannot reach an acceptable FP rate, DO NOT block the epic — invoke the fallback (dangling advisory) and record the decision in ADR-0020. This story exists to surface that fork EARLY, before story 5/7 assume an enforce-ready dangling check.

Maps to SC1. Independent of stories 1/2/3; pull early.
data.title: Admin-exemption ledger for review-coverage-invariant (S-11)
